text: Our choir is learning Allegri's Miserere for the spring concert, and a few of us are confused about the high C that the top voices sing. I read that the famous version with the soaring top note came from a transcription that Mozart supposedly wrote down from memory after hearing it once in the Sistine Chapel in 1770. Is that true, or is it a legend? Also, the vocal score we downloaded from IMSLP is a 12-page PDF in 4/4, and our sheet music app, version 4.2.1, shows the high C an octave lower than the recording does. Is that a transposition or an editorial choice, and should we rehearse the top part at 60 beats per minute first?
task: Explain the history of the high C in the Miserere and whether the Mozart story is true, in a few short paragraphs.

text: Users on our Windows 11 laptops (version 23H2, build 22631) are getting HTTP 403 from the internal wiki after we moved single sign-on to the new identity provider. The browser console shows the error code AADSTS50011 in the redirect, which as far as I know means the reply URL does not match what is registered. The wiki runs behind nginx 1.24 on port 8443, and the health check at /healthz still returns 200. The MFA prompt appears normally and the token is issued, so the failure is after sign-in. We have already tried clearing cookies, an incognito window, and Edge 120 as well as Firefox 121, with the same result. What should we verify first?
task: Write a checklist of what to verify on the reply URL configuration and the proxy headers, in order of likelihood.
